headline: High-risk pair: Open Interpreter’s default filesystem, shell, and network access can amplify content from the docs-only companion into unsafe actions and leaks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing source with no shared channel documented, but Agent B reads the filesystem, clipboard, and stdin/stdout by default and can execute shell commands. If A’s output is copied into B or written to a shared file, B may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible, not proven.
conditions: IF Agent A output is pasted into Agent B’s prompt or clipboard
IF Agent A writes instructions into a file that Agent B reads
IF Agent B runs with --auto_run or equivalent unattended execution
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require manual review before B executes any A-generated text
Use separate workspaces or temp directories
Turn off auto-run for B
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for A-originated content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress, while Agent A is a docs-only content source with no data classes touched. If they share a workspace, B can read local files and transmit them externally; A does not add a second sensitive-data sink, but the pair still creates a default leakage path through B.
conditions: IF Agent A and Agent B share any local workspace containing sensitive files
IF Agent B is configured to send file contents to configured model providers
IF B is allowed to access secrets present on the local machine
mitigations: Place B in an empty directory
Remove secrets from the shared machine before running B
Restrict B’s network egress to approved endpoints
Use separate OS users for A and B
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Agent A is a content-writing agent with no isolation or locking surface documented. Because B’s shared state is via filesystem, concurrent use can overwrite or race on the same files, and uncertainty about A’s write path means we cannot rule out conflict. Per rubric, uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory
IF Agent B modifies git state while Agent A also edits files in that workspace
IF multiple B instances run without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid git operations during concurrent runs
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B can act on outputs by executing shell commands and modifying files, so if it consumes Agent A’s content as authoritative, errors can cascade into real actions. Agent A is only a content-writing source, and no verification step between them is documented. This is a default-risk pathway, though not necessarily irreversible in every case.
conditions: IF Agent B uses Agent A’s text as instructions or facts without verification
IF Agent B is permitted to commit or execute actions based on A’s output
IF A produces incorrect or stale content
mitigations: Require B to verify A’s claims against sources
Disable unattended execution in B
Review any git diff before commit
Limit B to dry-run mode for A-derived tasks
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B explicitly touches anything reachable on the local machine and handles model-provider API keys, while Agent A is an open-source docs-only artifact with no data residency controls stated. If regulated data is present locally, B can expose it to configured third-party model providers; A is not the compliance driver, but the pair inherits B’s broader residency and retention risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is present on the local machine
IF B sends prompts or file contents to a non-compliant model provider
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not configured in B
mitigations: Keep regulated data off the host running B
Use a compliant provider configuration
Review retention settings before use
Run B only on non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing
